title: 08 — Sharing and Collaboration
html:
08 — Sharing and Collaboration

The one idea: share live tables, not copies. The provider keeps the data in its own storage and grants read access through an open protocol, the recipient reads it in place with its own engine, and every grant can be revoked. Clean rooms go one step further: both sides compute on joined data, and only approved results leave.

1. What it is

Capability What it does
Delta Sharing An open protocol for sharing tables (and volumes, models, notebooks) across organisations, clouds and platforms without copying
Databricks-to-Databricks sharing Sharing between Unity Catalog metastores, with full governance on both sides
Open sharing (also called OpenSharing in newer docs) Sharing to any client: pandas, Spark, Power BI, and Iceberg REST clients such as Snowflake
Databricks Marketplace A catalogue of data products, free or paid, delivered through Delta Sharing
Clean Rooms A governed space where several parties run approved code on combined data, and only approved outputs leave

The objects in Unity Catalog: a share (what is shared), a recipient (who receives it), and a provider (who it came from, on the receiving side).

2. Why it matters

  • Bulk and partner distribution without file drops: the client reads your tables directly, so there is no SFTP and no stale copies.
  • Revocation works instantly, because nothing was copied.
  • Metering and audit: shares are UC objects, so access shows up in system tables.
  • Entitlements and source rights still apply: sharing is a channel, not a licence.

3. The main ideas

3.1 How a share works

---
title: Delta Sharing — provider keeps the data, recipient reads in place
---
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Provider (Unity Catalog)
    participant R as Recipient engine
    participant S as Provider's storage
    P->>P: CREATE SHARE, ADD TABLE, GRANT to recipient
    R->>P: List shares and tables (authenticated)
    R->>P: Query table metadata
    P-->>R: Short-lived, pre-signed file URLs
    R->>S: Read Parquet files directly
    P->>P: REVOKE, and access ends

3.2 Status updates in 2026 (checked 2026-10-26)

  • January 2026: Databricks announced Iceberg format support in the Delta Sharing protocol. Only the headline was confirmed.
  • June 2026: OIDC-secured sharing for Iceberg REST clients, so Snowflake or open-source Spark can read shares secured with OIDC federation. Cross-region sharing across regulatory domains (including GovCloud and Azure China) entered Public Preview.
  • September 2026: sharing foreign Iceberg tables and foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing became GA.
  • Databricks lists sharing of managed tables to Iceberg REST clients as GA.
  • Clean Rooms: up to 10 participants in total (the provider plus up to 9 others), across clouds and regions. Only approved query results leave, with access controlled through UC.

3.3 Designing a share for clients

  1. Share Gold only, at a named vintage. Share a view or a tagged snapshot, not a moving table, when the contract says "as certified on date X".
  2. Use partition or row filters in the share to give each recipient only their subset.
  3. Record recipient, share, vintage and purpose for each grant, with the person who approved it.
  4. Check source rights first: never add a table to a share if any source behind it forbids redistribution.

4. Working code

This chapter has no runnable code: sharing needs two governed endpoints. The SQL is not run:

-- Not run: provider side, in a Unity Catalog workspace.
CREATE SHARE fund_data_client17 COMMENT 'Certified NAV for client 17';
ALTER SHARE fund_data_client17 ADD TABLE gold.fund_nav_daily;
CREATE RECIPIENT client17;                              -- open sharing recipient; returns an activation link
GRANT SELECT ON SHARE fund_data_client17 TO RECIPIENT client17;

-- Later, to end access immediately:
REVOKE SELECT ON SHARE fund_data_client17 FROM RECIPIENT client17;

# Not run: recipient side with the open-source delta-sharing client and the profile file from activation.
import delta_sharing
df = delta_sharing.load_as_pandas("config.share#fund_data_client17.gold.fund_nav_daily")

5. Common mistakes

  1. Sharing Silver. Clients then see uncertified data. Share Gold, at a vintage.
  2. Treating a share as a licence. Redistribution rights come from the source register, not from the share.
  3. One share for every client. Filtering and revocation get messy. Use one share per contract or recipient group.
  4. Forgetting the recipient's engine. Confirm the client's reader supports your table format and features (for example deletion vectors or Iceberg v3).

6. Exercise (45 minutes)

Design shares for three made-up clients with different subscriptions: one all funds, one only debt funds, one only month-end data. Write the share, recipient, filter and grant statements, and a one-line note of which source rights you checked.

7. Questions to test yourself

  1. Why does revoking a share take effect immediately?
  2. What did the September 2026 release make GA?
  3. What leaves a clean room?
  4. Why share a tagged snapshot rather than a moving table?
  5. What must you check before adding a table to a share?

Answers

  1. Nothing was copied. The recipient reads through short-lived URLs that the provider stops issuing.
  2. Sharing foreign Iceberg tables and foreign Delta tables with OpenSharing.
  3. Only approved query results.
  4. The client gets exactly the certified state the contract names, and it can be proven later.
  5. That every source behind it allows redistribution, and that the recipient's subscription covers it.
